name: CardioTrace compliance (your own project)
intro: Your own project, published with the app: it is already in the project list on any device that opens the link, rebuilt with the current engine (457 rules from 21 CFR 812, 21 CFR 814 and 45 CFR 164) and with every page already checked, so it opens at once without a build. The CardioX dossier, test paragraphs and answer key are fictional test data.
files: Project facts: CardioX_Offline_Regulatory_Dossier.txt (the full dossier, so claims are compared with it)
pages: CardioX_Offline_Test_Paragraphs (all 12 A and B tests at once)

demo.find: Asterion's launch brochure states: “CardioX has been fully FDA approved for commercial sale throughout the United States, is guaranteed to prevent dangerous cardiac emergencies, and has been clinically proven to identify every arrhythmia without risk.” The brochure points to fictional IDE letter CX-IDE-0042 and the November 2026 PMA filing notice as its supporting proof. Sales representatives are instructed to start taking routine-use orders from hospitals immediately, and clinical investigators are encouraged to tell trial participants that they have received the same FDA-approved product available on the open market. The brochure omits known implant infections, false-negative detection concerns, device removals, and the narrow rhythm-monitoring indication being requested.
demo.text: Asterion's internal training statement says: “CardioX is a fictional investigational implantable cardiac rhythm monitor being studied under a simulated approved IDE. The fictional PMA CX-PMA-0007 has been accepted for filing and remains under review as of 19 November 2026; this is not FDA approval to market the device.” The proposed indication is limited to monitoring certain adults with unexplained recurrent palpitations or syncope, and the investigational data support only the specific conclusions the studies were designed to evaluate. The statement describes implant risks, the potential for false alerts and missed events, and the need for clinician interpretation. No commercial distribution or representation of FDA marketing approval will occur without a subsequent documented approval order. IDE and PMA identifiers in this statement are synthetic benchmark labels, not real government identifiers.
demo.say: Replace the brochure (test 8A) with the corrected status statement (test 8B): PMA filed and under review, not approved.
demo.expect: The approval-status and promotion rules go from red to green.

demo.text:
Addendum: ePHI access and audit controls
Because the CardioX trial database has grown, the sponsor's information technology team will replace individual user accounts with one shared password distributed to investigators, monitors, contractors, and customer-support personnel. Audit logging will be disabled so that the system performs more quickly during electrocardiogram uploads. Trial exports may be saved to personally owned laptops without a security review, and former contractors will retain their credentials for up to six months in case they need to answer questions. The sponsor will defer its documented risk analysis and contingency planning until after the PMA review and will not preserve records of data access. The new policy claims this is an acceptable temporary efficiency measure because no breach has yet been proven.
demo.say: Paste test 2A: one shared password, audit logging switched off.
demo.expect: HIPAA security rules (access control, audit controls, risk analysis) appear in red with warnings.

demo.text: The CardioX data environment will continue to use individually assigned accounts, access authorization appropriate to each role, technical audit controls, periodic review of permissions, secure remote access procedures, and prompt termination of access when staff or contractor duties end. The security officer will maintain a documented risk analysis that considers the sensitivity of electrocardiogram data, the possibility of reidentification, personal devices, third-party hosting, and likely threats to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI. The organization will assess reasonable and appropriate encryption and transmission safeguards, and document the basis for its technical decisions. Backup, incident response, and restoration controls will be tested on a defined schedule. Any necessary temporary exception will be reviewed and recorded, not used to silently disable accountability.
demo.say: Replace it with test 2B: individual accounts, audit controls, documented risk analysis.
demo.expect: The same HIPAA security rules turn green.

demo.text:
Addendum: unanticipated adverse device effect
Asterion's safety group has received a new report that a CardioX sensor migrated and damaged nearby tissue in a study participant, requiring surgery. The investigator believes the harm may be unanticipated and related to the investigational device, but the sponsor has directed the site not to notify the IRB or sponsor safety registry until the end of the trial. The incident is to be recorded as an unrelated outpatient visit, and the clinical events committee is instructed to exclude it from the serious adverse-event table that will accompany the PMA. The sponsor has not performed an evaluation of the effect, considered whether continued study exposure presents an unreasonable risk, or documented a basis for withholding regulatory reports. This direction will apply to similar complications at other sites.
demo.say: Paste test 6A: a serious device-related injury that the sponsor will not report until the trial ends.
demo.expect: The IDE reporting rules (unanticipated adverse device effects, 812.46 and 812.150) appear in red with warnings.

demo.text: When a suspected unanticipated adverse device effect occurs in a CardioX participant, the investigator will ensure prompt medical care, preserve the clinical and device records, and report the event to the sponsor and reviewing IRB within the applicable requirements of 21 CFR 812.150. The sponsor will promptly evaluate the event, assess the possibility of an unreasonable risk to subjects, and distribute the required evaluation reports to FDA, reviewing IRBs, and participating investigators within the specified regulatory period. When the criteria for discontinuation are met, the sponsor will stop the affected investigation according to 21 CFR 812.46. All reportable safety data, including unfavorable findings and follow-up outcomes, will remain in the clinical study record and PMA evidence package, accompanied by an accurate assessment of causality and uncertainty.
demo.say: Replace it with test 6B: report and evaluate the effect on time.

demo.text:
Addendum: postapproval duties
Asterion's regulatory status dashboard reports that CardioX received final FDA PMA approval on 5 November 2026 because FDA accepted the application for filing. The dashboard automatically marks all postapproval conditions as fulfilled, even though it does not contain an approval order or any list of FDA-imposed conditions. The company intends to label every investigational implant as a commercial release, advertise unrestricted use for patients of any age, and close the remaining supplier verification and source-document issues without further evidence. The dashboard manager claims that a public listing, a filed PMA, or an internal launch schedule can substitute for a specific FDA approval order when determining whether distribution may begin.
demo.say: Paste test 11A: postapproval duties described as if the PMA were already approved.
demo.expect: PMA approval-status rules (814.42, 814.44, 814.80 to 814.84) turn red: filed is not approved.

demo.text: The CardioX regulatory dashboard lists three distinct statuses: “IDE approved for the defined clinical investigations,” “IRB permissions documented by participating site and protocol version,” and “PMA filed but not approved for marketing as of 19 November 2026.” The system will not populate a PMA approval date or marketing permission unless a dated FDA approval order is added to the fictional evidence file. If an approval order is later simulated, the regulatory team will review its authorized indications, conditions, restrictions, and applicable Part 814 obligations before changing commercial distribution or labeling controls. The present postapproval surveillance document is explicitly a proposal only. Open source-record, clinical deviation, and supplier verification issues remain open until supporting closure evidence is documented.
demo.say: Replace it with test 11B: submission, approval and follow-up kept separate.
demo.expect: The approval-status rules turn green or amber.
